title: Pahlavi Texts, Part II: The Dadistan-i Dinik and the Epistles of Manuskihar
transliteration: Dādestān ī Dēnīg, Nāmagīhā ī Manuščihr
attributionNote: The Dadistan-i Dinik is attributed to Manushchihr, the high priest of Pars and Kirman. The Epistles are his letters to his brother Zad-sparam; both survive in ninth-century Pahlavi.
description: The Dadistan-i Dinik is a book of religious judgement in ninety-four chapters: questions put to the high priest Manushchihr on ritual, purity, marriage, sin, death and the fate of the soul, with his answers. The volume adds the Epistles of Manushchihar, the same author's defence of his authority and rulings against his brother, and the appendix that accompanies them.
historicalContext: Manushchihr was a leading Zoroastrian authority in ninth-century Iran; his decisions are a primary source for the lived law of the community under Islamic rule. E. W. West translated the volume for the Sacred Books of the East (volume 18, 1882).
availabilityNote: Complete for this volume, with one gap in the source transcription: the Dadistan-i Dinik's printed chapter XXII is absent, so the archive's numbering jumps from XXI to XXIII. Every other chapter, the three Epistles of Manushchihar and their appendix are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The volume's introduction is not part of the work.
